$comment: The HDF OSCAL extension vocabulary (ADR-0014 §1.5): every prop an hdf-libs OSCAL exporter emits or importer reads by name, with the namespace it belongs to. The Go oscal package embeds this file and the TypeScript peer imports it; it is the only place a prop name or the HDF namespace URI is defined. 'objects' are OSCAL JSON paths; 'hdfField' is the HDF path the prop carries, or null when it carries none; 'legacy' is true exactly for the names exporters emitted without ns before ADR-0014, which the read helpers accept without ns for one minor release (§1.4).

props.name: hdf-requirement-id
props.meaning: The HDF requirement id the finding assesses, exactly as the source recorded it. The finding target-id carries an OSCAL token encoding of it, which is not injective.

props.name: baseline-version
props.meaning: The version of the HDF baseline the result reports.

props.name: nist
props.meaning: A NIST SP 800-53 control the requirement maps to, one prop per mapping, in source order.
props.valueFormat: String (§1.7), NIST control notation as the source spelled it

props.name: cci
props.meaning: A DISA Control Correlation Identifier the requirement maps to, one prop per mapping, in source order.

props.name: control-type
props.meaning: The requirement's control type.
props.valueFormat: One of policy, procedure, technical, management, operational

props.name: verification-method
props.meaning: How the requirement is verified.
props.valueFormat: One of automated, manual-by-design, manual-pending-automation, hybrid

props.name: applicability
props.meaning: Whether the requirement is required, optional or advisory.

props.name: cwe
props.meaning: A CWE identifier associated with the requirement, one prop per identifier, in source order.

props.name: epss-score
props.meaning: The EPSS exploitation probability score.

props.name: epss-percentile
props.meaning: The EPSS percentile of the score.

props.name: kev
props.meaning: The vulnerability is in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; emitted only when it is.

props.name: kev-due-date
props.meaning: The remediation due date the KEV catalog sets for the vulnerability.
props.valueFormat: String (§1.7), a date as the source recorded it

props.name: cvss-base-score
props.meaning: A CVSS base score, one prop per CVSS record that carries one, in source order.

props.name: cvss-base-vector
props.meaning: A CVSS base vector, one prop per CVSS record that carries one, in source order.

props.name: reference
props.meaning: A requirement reference that is plain text rather than a URL or URI (those become finding links).

props.name: check
props.meaning: Pre-ADR only: a one-line preview of the requirement's check text, with the full text in remarks. No longer emitted; the check text is carried in observation relevant-evidence marked with description-label.

props.name: fix
props.meaning: Pre-ADR only: a one-line preview of the requirement's fix text when no risk was emitted, with the full text in remarks. No longer emitted; the fix text is carried in a risk remediation or observation relevant-evidence marked with description-label.

props.name: rationale
props.meaning: Pre-ADR only: a one-line preview of the requirement's rationale text, with the full text in remarks. No longer emitted; the rationale is carried in the finding target description.

props.name: description-label
props.meaning: Marks the object as carrying the text of the HDF description with this label; evidence entries hold the full text in remarks, remediations in description.

props.name: empty-field
objects: Any object that carries HDF props
props.meaning: An optional HDF string field that is present but empty; the importer returns it present and empty (§1.7.3).
props.valueFormat: The name of the HDF field

props.name: absent-field
objects: Any object that carries HDF props
props.meaning: OSCAL requires a value the HDF field does not have, so the object holds display fallback text; the importer leaves the field absent and never reads the fallback as HDF data (§1.7.4).
props.valueFormat: The name of the HDF field

props.name: amendment-id
props.meaning: The identifier of the HDF amendments document.

props.name: override-type
props.meaning: The type of the HDF override the risk represents.
props.valueFormat: An HDF override type, such as waiver, poam or falsePositive

props.name: impact-override
props.meaning: The impact the override assigns to the requirement.

props.name: justification
props.meaning: The controlled-vocabulary justification for the override.

props.name: baseline-ref
props.meaning: The baseline the override is scoped to.

props.name: component-ref
props.meaning: The component the override is scoped to.

props.name: milestone-status
props.meaning: The status of the milestone the remediation represents.

props.name: completed-at
props.meaning: When the milestone was completed.

props.name: completed-by
props.meaning: The identifier of whoever completed the milestone.

props.name: mime-type
props.meaning: The media type of the evidence the observation carries.

props.name: captured-by
props.meaning: The identifier of whoever captured the evidence the observation carries.

props.name: source-name
props.meaning: The name of the source of the external reference the resource carries.

props.name: external-id
props.meaning: The identifier the source assigns to the external reference the resource carries.

props.name: impacted-control-id
props.meaning: FedRAMP vocabulary: a control impacted by the POA&M item. The POA&M exporter emits it and the importer reads it as the override requirement id.

props.name: POAM-ID
props.meaning: FedRAMP vocabulary: the CSP-assigned POA&M tracking identifier. The importer reads it as the override requirement id when no related risk carries impacted-control-id.

props.name: CORE
props.meaning: FedRAMP vocabulary: the control must be included in every FedRAMP assessment. The importer maps the value true to applicability required.

props.name: assessment-type
props.meaning: FedRAMP vocabulary: the type of assessment. The importer maps automated and manual to the plan type.

props.name: label
props.meaning: NIST vocabulary: a human-readable label for the control, which may be rendered in place of its identifier.

props.name: sort-id
props.meaning: NIST vocabulary: an alternative identifier that sorts easily among the other controls in the document.

props.name: version
props.meaning: NIST vocabulary: the version of the component. The importer reads it from the first assessment-asset component as the runner version.

props.name: type
props.meaning: NIST vocabulary: the kind of resource. HDF emits the value evidence on the resource holding a requirement's source code.
props.valueFormat: A NIST resource type; HDF emits evidence
